numerical_failure.observed_behavior: The residuals of a UECM model created with UECM.from_ardl subtract the fitted values of the UECM (in differences) from the ARDL endogenous value (in levels), so uecmfit.resid is not the same as the equivalent ARDL residuals (ardlfit.resid).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to the residuals in deriving the UECM from the ARDL; uecmfit.resid should equal ardlfit.resid.
trigger_conditions: Model created via statsmodels.tsa.ardl.UECM.from_ardl(ardl) from an ARDL model
Accessing the resid property of the fitted UECM result
Reproduction uses ARDL(S[:,[0]], 1, S[:,[1]], 1) with S a simulated cointegrated two-series array (unseeded in the issue)

category_specific_evidence: Issue #9323 states that UECM.from_ardl residuals subtract UECM fitted values (differences) from ARDL endog values (levels), so UECM residuals differ from the equivalent ARDL residuals.
Issue #9323 states the UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to residuals when deriving the UECM from the ARDL.
The fix overrides the resid property in the UECM results class to compute model._y minus self.fittedvalues, per the diff in statsmodels/tsa/ardl/model.py.
Reproduction compares uecmfit.resid against ardlfit.resid and checks that UECM endog equals the observed levels series S[:,0].
reproduction_risks: The reproduction script in the issue uses unseeded np.random.multivariate_normal, so exact residual values are not reproducible without a fixed seed, which the passages do not provide.
The issue's code sample is truncated in the passage, so the full simulation setup is not fully recoverable.
No concrete residual values or expected numerical tolerance are given in the passages.
